additions.text: Norma is eating in the hospital kitchen. She is talking on the phone with her sister Susana.
Hi, Susana! I'm eating a sandwich.
Oh, yes! A man says: "I'm the doctor's cousin."
No. And a woman says: "Today is my birthday."
Ha! And does she have a number?
No. There is no machine, there is no paper… and I have no sevens.
Which number does Norma not have?
Do you wait in lines patiently?
What do you eat at work?
Andrés arrives at the waiting room. Anselmo, a very friendly man, explains the rules.
Hi, I'm Anselmo. I've been here for eight hours.
Well, Andrés, there are three rules. One: the green chair is mine.
Two: the coffee is for everyone. Three: here we talk a lot.
And the man with the towel?
He's my friend. And he's next, for sure.
How many hours has Anselmo been waiting?
Do you talk to people you don't know?
Do you have a favorite chair at home?
What do you do when you wait?
Doña Pilar has a splinter in her finger. She calls her daughter Ximena on the phone.
Ximena, darling, I'm at the hospital. I have a splinter in my finger.
And there's no VIP chair. I'm a friend of the director!
Mom… your friend isn't the director. He's the waiter.
The waiter? But he's very elegant…
Yes. And he brings you dessert.
What does Pilar have in her finger?
What is there not in the room?
Gladys has hiccups and thinks she is dying. Wilson, the nurse, writes down her will.
Wilson, write, please. It's my will.
Gladys, you have hiccups. Nothing else.
My cat is for my sister. My soap operas are for my mom. Hic!
My ex's guitar… in the trash!
What color is Gladys's bracelet in the end?
Do you have a cat or a dog?
Doctor Íñigo has been at the hospital for a long time. Catalina talks to him in the corridor.
Íñigo, are you okay? Your eyes are red.
I'm perfect. Thirty hours here. Nine coffees.
Yes. And I call a patient Michi.
Oh… really? Well, the patient is very nice.
One more coffee and I'm leaving.
How many hours has he been at the hospital?
What does Íñigo want at the end?
How many coffees do you drink a day?
Does your pet have a funny name?
Yamilé and Manuel are resting in the ambulance. They talk about the day's strange calls.
Manuel, turn off the radio, please.
No! It's salsa. It's my music.
Today there are three strange calls. One: a man with a parrot on his head.
Two: a woman with her hand in a jar.
Oh, Kevin! Lots of phone and not much leg.
What does Yamilé want at the beginning?
What music does Manuel listen to?
Where does the woman have her hand?
Do you listen to music in the car?
Do you use your phone a lot?
Ezequiel has a broken arm. Paola, his neighbor, is with him. Paola has a secret.
A little. But your cat is fine.
The cat doesn't climb up alone. I put him up there. That way you come to my house.
Oh! My broken arm… and I'm happy.
Who puts the cat up the tree?
Do you have a small secret?
What do you do for love?
Don Benigno is better. His granddaughter Camila is with him. They talk about grandma.
Fine, thank you. Sorry for the scare, Camila.
You know? I think about your grandma. She always says: "Benigno, speak louder."
That's true! You speak very softly.
Yes. From today I speak loudly. Hello, nurse! Thank you very much!
Do you speak loudly or softly?
Do you say sorry a lot?
Rufino has a fishing hook in his eyebrow. He tells his story to Marta, the nurse.
Marta, it's a heroic story. There's a huge fish. Two meters long.
Two meters? And the hook in your eyebrow?
The fish is very strong. It pulls, pulls…
Rufino, your son says something else.
My son? What does he say?
He says: "Dad is my first fish."
For the son, who is his first fish?
Do you tell slightly false stories?
What do you do with your family on Sundays?
Federico is having a coffee. Doña Ramona has news: two people at the hospital are a couple.
Oh, Federico! A doctor and a doctor… they're a couple.
Clues: they're both surgeons. He's from Chile. She's from Colombia.
Doctor Undurraga and Doctor Ibarra? But they always argue!
Yes… and they always eat together. Two coffees, one dessert, two spoons.
What are Ramona and Federico talking about?
What job does the couple have?
Who do you usually eat with?
A few days later, Jorge calls Gonzalo on the phone. He doesn't want to pay the bill.
Hi, Gonzalo. I'm Jorge Treviño. The bill is a rip-off!
Calm down, Jorge. There's a new charge.
Call to billing: ten pesos per minute, plus five pesos for "hello".
Thank you, Jorge. That's fifteen pesos.
What is the bill for Jorge?
How much does one minute cost?
How much does Jorge pay for the call?
Do you pay many bills every month?
Do you call or write messages?
What is very expensive in your city?
Andrea reads Luis's blood-type horoscope. Luis doesn't believe in horoscopes.
Luis, your blood is O positive. Your horoscope: a tube breaks.
And a person from your family calls you.
See? And your lucky number is seven.
Oh! Tube number seven… is broken.
What blood type does Luis have?
Do you have a lucky number?
Does your mom call you a lot?
Karla has a ring in her stomach. Her friend Yolanda asks why.
My boyfriend sings at karaoke… with another girl. Five songs!
Yes. And now he wants the ring. It's his grandmother's.
I say: "The ring is in a very safe place."
How many songs does he sing with the girl?
Do you have a special ring?
Do you have a friend like Yolanda?
After the surgery, Lorenzo and Mercedes are in the changing room. They argue again.
Lorenzo, your opera is very sad.
And your reggaeton is very noisy, Mercedes.
Well… but your hands are very good.
But the vacation week is mine.
What are Lorenzo and Mercedes doing?
What is opera like for Mercedes?
What is very good about both of them?
What do they argue about at the end?
Do you like opera or reggaeton?
Do you argue with your coworkers?
How many weeks of vacation do you have?
Doctor Rodrigo explains to Tania his tricks for sleeping at the hospital.
Tania, my trick number one: I sleep with socks on.
It's science. Trick number two: I sleep five minutes on every sofa.
My worst day: I sleep in the elevator. Six hours. Up, down, up…
How many minutes does he sleep on each sofa?
Where does he sleep on his worst day?
Do you sleep with socks on?
How many hours do you sleep?
Margarita is finishing her shift. Roberto is starting. Margarita explains the rooms.
Roberto, there are fourteen call bells. Room four hundred four: wants the TV remote.
Four hundred five: a man wants to marry the nurse.
Four hundred seven. The lady has a fever. Her first.
How many call bells are there?
What does the man in four hundred five want?
Do you do many things at once?
Do you watch TV a lot?
Do you work during the day or at night?
Don Mario is smoking on the stairs with his IV. Lorena, from cleaning, finds him again.
Don Mario, here again. With your IV and your gown open.
Lorena, it's my cigarette number three. Today is the last one.
And you? Don't you have a vice?
Yes. Chocolate. And the stories of the corridors.
What is Mario doing on the stairs?
Do you have a small vice?
Do you like other people's stories?
It's the morning after Doña Karina's party. Juan, her roommate, is awake.
Good morning, Juan. Sorry about the party.
Good morning, Karina. Well… the cake is very good.
Yes, I have four. And you?
I have nine grandchildren. And they all dance badly!
Ha! I dance very well. My wife says no.
Then next year you dance with me.
How many grandchildren does Karina have?
It's night in the ICU. Paloma is with her dad. She talks with Doctor Carlos Zelaya.
Carlos, why do you work here?
My mom is a nurse. She says: "Life is here, Carlos."
How nice. My dad is very stubborn.
Well… but his heart is strong today.
Really? Oh, thank you! Dad, do you hear? Your heart is stubborn too.
What do Paloma and Carlos talk about?
How is the dad's heart today?
What job does your mom have?
Do you talk a lot with your dad?
Sofía is new. Don Marcelo explains the house rules to her.
Sofía, there are three rules here. Rule one: you always say "good morning" to the clients.
They're shy. Rule two: my lunch is in the blue fridge. Not in the gray fridge.
Rule three: the radio with boleros. Always.
What do you say to the clients?
What music is on the radio?
What do you eat for lunch?
Are you afraid of the dark?
Do you listen to old music?
Sofía is looking for the pharmacy. Doña Lorena is cleaning the corridor and has a special map.
Doña Lorena, where is the pharmacy?
Look, sweetheart. This is my map. Here, in the closet, Doctor Rodrigo sleeps.
Yes. Elevator three never comes. And Don Mario smokes on the stairs.
Ah! The pharmacy… is closed. Always.
Do you know your city well?
Do you use the elevator or the stairs?
Do you have a secret place?
You walk into the hospital. There are a lot of people. The number machine is broken.
Hi. My eye is blue. What number am I?
No number, no doctor. That’s the rule.
I write the numbers myself. But I’m out of sevens.
Norma looks at you: “Do you have a number?”
Norma hugs you. The man with the peas cries.
No. But the man is in pain.
Everybody is in pain. It’s a hospital.
The man waits. The peas aren’t cold anymore.
What about a kick to the machine?
Ha, ha. It has ten years of kicks.
You kick it. A number comes out: zero.
Are there a lot of queues in your city?
Do you always follow the rules?
You are in the waiting room. Don Anselmo has a sore throat. He has been here for eight hours.
Hi, new guy. Coffee? It’s free. Well, it’s my coffee.
No. I’m the king of the room. A bet? Who goes in next?
Anselmo looks at you: “Are you in?”
Yes. Five pesos on the lady with the dog.
Good choice! She coughs a lot.
The lady goes in. You win ten pesos and a cold coffee.
Why don’t you go home, Don Anselmo?
There’s nobody at home. Here there are friends.
Anselmo looks at a photo of his wife. Andrés holds his hand.
No, thanks. And you, go home!
Home? But tomorrow it’s my turn!
Anselmo doesn’t go home. Now there’s a bet on you.
What do you do when you wait?
Do you talk to people you don’t know?
Do you live alone or with other people?
In the good chairs sits Doña Pilar. She has a tiny splinter in her finger. Next to her, a tired man in a grey cardigan. He is the director, but nobody knows.
I’m a friend of the director! I want a doctor now!
Hello. I’m nobody. I’m just waiting.
Pilar looks at you: “Do you know who I am?”
Yes, madam. You are very important.
Pilar gives you her card. It’s a restaurant’s card.
Do you know the man in the cardigan?
That one? No. He’s a normal man.
Alonso smiles and writes “Pilar” in his notebook.
Alonso says: “I think the hospital needs chairs.” Pilar turns red.
Do you know a famous person?
Do you pay more to be first?
Gladys has hiccups. On the internet she reads: “hiccups, death.” She has a will on a napkin.
I’m dying! I want the red bracelet!
You have hiccups, madam. Green bracelet.
Hic! Green? Green is hope, not death!
Gladys looks at you: “Will you help me with my will?”
No? Then why am I scared? Hic!
Wilson gives you a green bracelet too.
The cat is for you! And the guitar too.
Now you have a cat, a guitar and a napkin.
It’s your last day. What do you do?
I dance, I eat cake and I call my ex! Hic!
Gladys dances in the corridor. The hiccups are gone.
Do you look everything up on the internet?
Which colour do you like most?
Do you have a cat or a dog?
What do you do on a day off?
You are in the emergency ward. Doctor Íñigo has been working for thirty hours. His eyes are red.
Good morning… or good night? Mr Michi, open your mouth.
I’m Pedro. Michi is your cat.
No. My prescription: one coffee. Two coffees. Three.
Íñigo looks at you: “Do you have coffee?”
Yes, a big coffee for you.
I love you! And what’s your name, cat?
Íñigo works two more hours. Catalina is not happy.
Íñigo falls asleep on a chair. Catalina puts a blanket on him.
How many hours do you work?
Do you drink a lot of coffee?
What are you like when you are sleepy?
What time do you get up?
An ambulance arrives. Yamilé and Manuel bring Kevin. Kevin has blood on his leg and his phone in his hand.
Hi, friends! I’m in the hospital! A thousand people watching!
Yamilé looks at you: “Do you have an idea?”
Kevin shouts: “More light!” Now you are his camera.
No more phone. Give me that.
Kevin cries. A thousand people say “bye”. The leg is happy.
Now there are ten thousand people. They all look at your face, not the leg.
Do you use your phone a lot?
What is your favourite social network?
Do you have a bike or a motorbike?
Ezequiel has a broken arm and blood on his forehead. Doctor Catalina puts on the cast.
The cat is up there. I go up. The ladder doesn’t.
The cat comes down by itself. Very calm.
Ezequiel! My hero! Tigre is fine.
Ezequiel looks at you, red-faced: “Paola is very pretty, isn’t she?”
Me? Well… Paola, I like you.
Paola smiles. The cat gets out of the box and leaves.
Paola, the cat isn’t in any trouble.
Paola says: “I know.” Ezequiel doesn’t understand a thing.
It’s sunny… and Paola is the sun.
Catalina rolls her eyes and finishes the cast.
What do you do for love?
In observation there is a lot of noise. Don Benigno is very pale. His granddaughter Camila is at the cafeteria.
Excuse me. Sorry to bother you.
I think I’m dying a little bit. But it’s not urgent.
Benigno looks at you: “Do you have a minute?”
Oh, thank you… and sorry about the noise.
Five people run over. Benigno is OK. He says sorry to everyone.
Yes. Take my hand. I’ll call Camila.
Your hand is warm. Thank you.
Camila comes running with two coffees. Benigno smiles.
What do you want to tell your family?
That I love them. And that the dog eats my socks.
You write it all down. A doctor arrives in time. The dog is in trouble.
Do you talk a lot or a little?
Do you say “I love you” to your family?
Do you say sorry a lot?
Who listens to you when you feel bad?
Rufino has a fishing hook in his eyebrow. There is a little blood. Nurse Marta gets the tweezers ready.
My son goes fishing for the first time. His first fish… is Dad.
The fish is fine. Very fine.
Rufino looks at you: “Now or in three minutes?”
Marta has the hook. Rufino wants it for his house.
Leo. He’s seven and he’s… OW!
The hook is out. Rufino says: “It doesn’t hurt.” It hurts a little.
Rufino posts the photo online. It gets a hundred likes.
Do you have children or nephews and nieces?
What do you do at weekends?
Do you prefer the countryside or the beach?
Do you have a ridiculous photo?
You are in the cafeteria. The menu has been the same for twenty years. A surgeon eats standing up, with blood on his clothes.
Today there’s soup. Soup of the day.
Ramona looks at you: “And for you, sweetheart?”
The soup is green. It’s tasty. You don’t know what it is.
Oh, yes. The machine is my bank.
Ramona gives you free bread. The machine eats another coin.
Love, lots of salt… and something else.
Federico whispers: “The something else is yesterday’s soup.”
What do you eat when you’re sad?
Do you eat standing up or sitting down?
Is there a gossip at your work?
the set menu of the day
Gonzalo works in billing. He is very polite. Jorge has his bill and he is not happy.
Chair: six hours, a hundred pesos. Air: fifty pesos.
Air? I pay for the air?
And a nurse’s smile: twenty pesos.
Gonzalo looks at you: “And you? How are you paying?”
The air? I don’t breathe much.
Jorge doesn’t breathe much either. He pays thirty.
I’ll pay it all. I want to go home.
Very good! And ten pesos for paying.
You leave with no money, but with a very pretty receipt.
Yes. The form costs five pesos.
Jorge writes a three-page complaint: fifteen pesos.
What is very expensive in your country?
Do you pay by card or in cash?
You are in the lab. Andrea labels the tubes. Luis is tired. A machine makes a lot of noise.
This blood is A positive. Today is a good day for love.
Luis is O negative. Always negative.
Andrea looks at you: “What’s your blood type?”
I don’t know. What does my horoscope say?
The cafeteria only has fish. Today you don’t eat.
That’s what a B negative would say, of course.
Luis shakes your hand. Now you two are a team.
You buy a lottery ticket. You win… a plastic tube.
Are you a positive or a negative person?
Karla is in radiology. She doesn’t want to give the ring back to her ex. So the ring is in her stomach.
Here is the ring. And a key. And a very old coin.
The key… it’s my house key!
I don’t know. It’s from before.
Karla looks at you: “So what do I do now?”
Give it back? How? Which way out?
Karla and Yolanda laugh a lot. The ex doesn’t want the ring.
It’s your ring. It’s fine there.
Karla pats her belly lovingly. Her stomach isn’t so happy.
Karla calls. The ex says: “And my key?”
Do you have a special gift from someone?
Do you talk to your exes?
What is in your pockets today?
You are upstairs, behind a glass window, with Tania. Below, two surgeons operate and argue.
Look. Now they don’t talk. They work perfectly.
Done. And the holiday week is mine!
Tania looks at you: “What music would you put on?”
The surgeons dance a little. The patient is fine.
Lorenzo and Mercedes look up. Tania is under the chair.
Mercedes wins. Tania pays with a sweet.
Do you listen to music when you work?
Do you argue with your colleagues?
You are in the staff room. Doctor Rodrigo is on the sofa, under a blanket. His pager beeps. Someone is heating up fish.
I’m not here. Rodrigo isn’t here.
It’s a dream. You are a dream.
Tania looks at you: “What do I do with him?”
Rodrigo sleeps for two hours. Tania does the work of two.
Rodrigo goes to the operating room with the blanket on his head.
Well… I’ll lie down on the sofa too.
Now the sofa has two people and one blanket.
What do you do to relax?
You are at the nurses’ station. There are fourteen call bells. Margarita is very calm. Roberto arrives for the night shift.
Four-oh-four: the TV remote. Four-oh-five: a wedding. Four-oh-six: the wifi password.
Yes. He’s ninety. She’s eighty-nine. It’s urgent.
Margarita looks at you: “Will you help me?”
Yes. I’ll take care of the wifi.
Room four-oh-six is happy. The others aren’t.
Tea, deep breaths and lots of silence.
Bell number fifteen rings. Margarita’s face doesn’t change.
Roberto opens the door: the robot asks for a glass of water.
Do you do many things at once?
Do you find it easy to say “no”?
What’s your wifi password? Just kidding: do you like technology?
In the corridor, Don Mario walks with his drip and a gown open at the back. He’s going to the stairs. He wants to smoke.
Don Mario, again. And everything is showing, you know?
At my age, it doesn’t matter.
Mario looks at you: “Got a light?”
No. Back to your room, Don Mario.
Oh, you’re worse than my wife.
Mario goes back to bed. The cigarette is under the pillow.
I don’t smoke, but I’ll keep you company.
You talk about his youth. Lorena brings three coffees.
One cigarette today, and zero tomorrow.
The next day, Mario says: “Today is another day.”
Do you have a bad habit?
What is hard for you to give up?
What small pleasure do you have every day?
Are there smokers in your family?
Room four-oh-two. Doña Karina turns eighty today. There is cake, balloons, music and twelve cousins.
Madam, please. My operation was yesterday.
I can’t eat. Or sleep. Or escape.
Karina looks at you: “Will you dance with me?”
You dance with Karina. Juan puts the pillow over his head.
Quiet? There’s quiet in the cemetery.
Karina turns the music down… a little. Juan says “thank you”.
One more song and then, quiet.
The song lasts twenty minutes. Juan learns the lyrics.
How do you celebrate your birthday?
Do you share a room with someone?
You are in the ICU. It is very quiet. Paloma’s dad is asleep. He has a lot of machines.
Dad, your sister has a new boyfriend. He’s ugly.
And your team is losing. Three-nil. I’m sorry… no, I’m not sorry.
He can hear. Keep talking, keep talking.
Paloma looks at you: “Is it silly to talk to him?”
I don’t say anything. I just listen.
Thank you. It’s good not to be alone.
Paloma holds her dad’s hand. The machines go “beep”.
It’s not silly. Talk some more.
OK. Dad, the dog is eating your shoes.
The number on the monitor goes up a little. Doctor Carlos smiles.
He’s grumpy, funny… and my best friend.
Paloma talks about her dad for an hour. She laughs and cries.
Who do you talk to a lot in your family?
Is there a team you really don’t like?
What words do you like to hear?
Do you call your parents a lot?
You are in the morgue. It is cold. Don Marcelo eats his lunch and listens to boleros. Sofía, the new intern, is scared.
Good morning, gentlemen. All well? Very quiet, as always.
With my clients. But this tag belongs to a living man. He’s on the second floor.
Marcelo looks at you: “Are you hungry?”
Cold chicken. Everything here is cold.
You eat with Marcelo. Sofía watches, white as a sheet.
You run down the corridor. Sofía runs behind you.
Today. A living client. It’s a problem.
You go up to the second floor. The living man reads his tag and screams.
Are you afraid of the dark?
Do you know a very strange job?
What do you eat for lunch?
Do you talk to plants or animals?
In the service corridor, Doña Lorena mops blood off the floor. A stretcher goes by. A doctor runs. She is calm.
Excuse me, where is the lift?
Lift three never comes. Use number one.
And in room twelve there is a secret.
Lorena looks at you: “And what do you want, sweetheart?”
Oh! Someone is helping me. It’s a miracle.
You clean together. Lorena tells you three secrets.
A doctor, a nurse and a pizza.
Sofía opens the door. Everyone is eating pizza. Nobody is working.
Thirty years here, sweetheart. Everything is normal.
A goat walks down the corridor. Lorena keeps mopping.
Who in your life works hard and nobody notices?
What is the hardest day of your week?
